says: The interface evaluation set (spec 01, design §4): each case's inputs and its expected numbers, worked out by hand from the sources of §2.3 before the code ran (ISO 273, DIN 974-1, ISO 4762 in threads.ts, ISO 2306, Bossard's engagement lengths, ISO 286-1's Table 1, NEMA ICS 16 in kinds/motion.ts, the insert maker's table). Sizes in mm.

cases.what: an M8 socket cap screw through a 10 mm steel plate, medium fit
cases.worked: ISO 273 medium for M8: 9.0; DIN 974-1 series 1 for M8: 15; depth the ISO 4762 head's k 8 and 0.5 (typical) = 8.5, within the 10 mm plate

imprint.worked: in the middle of a 100 mm plate: its edge 50 mm from the 9 mm hole (EN 1993-1-8 asks 1.2 × 9 = 10.8); no other hole; the counterbore 8.5 mm within its 10 mm

cases.what: an M6 screw into 6061 aluminium, plate 8 mm
cases.worked: 6061-T6 Rm 310 MPa (the handbook): Bossard's aluminium row over 180 MPa gives 2.0 d for 8.8, so 12 mm of thread; the plate is 8: refused

imprint.worked: its depth measured along its line, 8 mm; the thread asks 12 (Bossard): refused before anything else

cases.what: an M4 screw into a PLA part 10 mm thick
cases.worked: a polymer: no thread cut; CNC Kitchen's TC-M4x8.1 insert (8.1 mm long, 6.3 mm across) in its 5.7 mm hole, blind L + 1 = 9.1 mm deep, within the 10 mm part; the insert placed as a part

cases.what: an M8 hole 4 mm from a plate's edge

imprint.worked: the hole ISO 273 medium, d0 9.0 mm; EN 1993-1-8 Table 3.3 asks e2 ≥ 1.2 d0 = 10.8 mm; the edge is 50 − 46 = 4 mm from its line: refused, 6.8 mm short
an M8 hole of 9.0 mm already at the middle; the new one 15 mm from it; EN 1993-1-8 asks p1 ≥ 2.2 d0 = 19.8 mm: refused

cases.what: a NEMA 17 motor onto a 5 mm plate
cases.worked: NEMA 17's face: four M3 on a 31 mm square, a 22 mm pilot; ISO 273 medium for M3: 3.4; the pilot's bore 22 H7: 0 to +21 µm (ISO 286-1 Table 1, IT7 at 18 to 30 mm)

cases.what: two plates (10 and 6 mm) bolted, M8

fastener.worked: grip 16; ISO 7089 washers 1.6 each; ISO 4032 nut 6.8; two pitches 2.5: 28.5 mm; the shortest ISO 4017 M8 length sold at or above it, 30 mm

follows.worked: M8's hole 9.0 mm (ISO 273 medium); EN 1993-1-8 asks 1.2 d0 = 10.8 mm from the bore's edge to each hole's centre: the bolt circle at least 20 + 10.8 = 30.8 mm round; the bore made 50 mm, 25 + 10.8 = 35.8 mm; six holes in the flange and the cover at that radius; the bolts through 10 + 6 mm as case 8 works it, bolt M8x30; widening the bore runs the bore, the radius, the circle, both parts' holes and the bolts again, and not the two plates

cases.what: a box made 10 mm taller after an imprint on its top

reapply.worked: the imprint at x 10, z −20 mm on the top of a 100 × 10 × 100 plate; the plate made 20 mm tall about its middle: its top is now at y = 10 mm, so the imprint is made again there and its hole runs the new 20 mm; one cut, the old one gone. The plate made 15 mm wide: x = 10 mm is off it, no face answers: lost. The plate made a ball: the surface there faces otherwise: lost.
